questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I've always wanted to do an exchange, particularly in Asia, I applied to South Korea in my bachelors but this feel through due to Covid. I was ecstatic to be admitted into a university such as Fudan, a top school in a profoundly exciting country. The ability to be in one of the most populated cities learning things that are not necessarily provided within the Asian context.

Academically felt very rewarding.

Socially, it was nice to be able to be in a social bubble in the Fudan university campus. 
Being in fudan, living on the campus was just about english friendly and international enough, which was a big costernation before coming here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't particularly straightforward due to language barriers, both interpersonal and through accessing the websites. Things were often hard to understand in english and this could be work on more. Luckily I made friends who were familiar/could speak chinese

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Had help getting to the dorm from the airport.

The orientation day was useful for getting the intitial, important information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: English was not a strong suit so I can't give an extremely high mark

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: International student dorm. I was in a double room, but I'm sure single rooms are also an option

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Excellent food options in a massive cafeteria, cheap and tasty and easily accessible

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It's next to impossible to change rooms, so make sure you try to get the right kind of room that you want and be wary of roommate dynamics as the room is quite crammed and initimate (not for everyone).

Not very close to the city center, but everything is set up nicely.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had my own roommate problems, but price, comfort and accessibility wise it all ranks excellently.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite straightforward and helpful staff that were quick to respond.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After being nominated by KU, it was about 2 months of back and forth with Fudan, accomodated by forms and submiission of further files and pdfs. Still quite straightforward, the only hard part was getting everything confirmed in a timely manner.  It wasn't until about 2 months before embarking on the exchange that I was certain that I could leave for China with everything set in place. This could affect price ticket's and one's planning of life, etc..

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Extremely, not many options, but I wasn't rejected from any classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
As mentioned above but make sure you do your research so that you know what to expect regarding language barriers, technical difficulties, try to learn some chinese for formalities at least. It is quite a different culture with different so be prepared for that. 
Complemented by the language barrier, It is a better destination for studying dilligently than partying I feel, which is perhaps not everyone's cup of tea for exchanges.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master courses specifcially from the International relations sphere, different from my Msc in Social Data Science.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I preffered it to be honest, mostly small scale, lecture based, relaxed and extremely informative. Reading amount/workload was similar but teachers were more accomodating.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Foreign Policy Analysis
- Sino-Russian relations
- Social policy (audited first half)
- Global Governance
- Chinese Foreign Economic Policy 
- Political Developments in Modern China (audited whole course)
- Comparative Perspective on International Regions

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the ones I partook in except for social Policy, which I began and stopped as it quite geared towards maths/quantative social sciences.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Should have bought more data than originally expected on my SIM card upon arriving, I often had to top up my data which added up. Also, the price of water should be considered as you can't drinkl from the sink.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less; Housing, transport (public and taxi), food (in canteen and most restaurants)

More: Clothes and cosmetic products

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Had access to the gym for free, wasn't particulary nice. 

No setting up of intenrational oppurtunities for sport clubs, clubbing and what no

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: not sure

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore shanghai (and China) as much as possible. It's incredibly impressive

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the main tourist attractions, its such a big city with so many impressive areas that one can feel like it is neverending, it's good to have a check-book for exploring the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Not that easy initially . Had I had hingsight, I would have prioritised learning as much basic Chinese as possible beforehand. 

It takes about 3 weeks to figure out how everything works, campus wise

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's tough due to language barrier and they are generally quite introverted, unbothered. While they speak english, it's probably better to look out for other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Introversion level,

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very smart people, extremely impressive city and culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Learn some chinese
- Get a room at the dorm and make sure that it is of your preference and that you are ready/able to share a small room with someone
- Make sure you stay close to a group of people and don't isolate yourself as it is quite cliquey on a whole

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being on the other side of the world, being so impressed by the city, the infrastructure and the way things are run, and being educated on China's rise and perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Should have learned some chinese as english was not enough usually (phones helped thoguh)
- sharing a small room with someone who was quite immature

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
